title: Migration Jurisprudence from the South: databases of migration and labor law
description:
Open, coded data on migration and labor law from the perspective of the Global South, published by the Institute for Migrant Rights at theimr.org/databases.

The archive holds every database as CSV, JSON and BibTeX files with codebooks (folder data/), and the website pages that explain the methods (folder site/):

  • Migration Law Atlas: international, regional and national instruments, ratifications, with a farmworker view
  • Court Decisions: judgments on migrant workers' rights, centred on courts in Asia, Africa, the Middle East and Latin America
  • Destination states compared: Gulf States, East Asia, Southeast Asia
  • Countries of Origin: emigration and protection law and policy
  • Migrant Domestic Workers: international, regional and national law
  • Government Hate Speech, with a comparison of hate speech, voting and the legal protection of non-citizens

Each database carries its own version number; the release notes list them. Each row links to an official source where one is available, and entries not yet checked against the official text are marked. The data are not legal advice.

License: CC BY 4.0 for the data and site text. Third-party material keeps its own terms (see LICENSE.md); court judgments and legislation are linked, not copied.
notes: Cite the release you used. Each database page at theimr.org gives a citation with that database's own version number.
